chunks: 1580 - Al-Riḍā ʿAlī ibn Mūsā عليه السلام wrote to Muḥammad ibn Sinān, in what he wrote to him as a response to his questions:

“The reason for zakat is for the sustenance of the poor and the safeguarding of the wealth of the rich, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has charged the people of health with attending to the affair of those afflicted with chronic disability and trial, just as Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said,
“You will surely be tested in your wealth and yourselves.”

In your wealth is the giving of zakat, and in yourselves is settling the souls upon patience, along with what is in that of rendering thanks for the blessings of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and hoping for increase, together with what it contains of increase, kindness, and mercy toward the people of weakness, tenderness toward the people of poverty, urging them toward mutual assistance, strengthening the poor, and helping them in the matter of religion. And it is an admonition for the people of wealth and a lesson for them, so that through them they may infer the poor of the Hereafter, and what there is for them in that of urging gratitude to Allah, Blessed and Exalted, for what He has entrusted to them and given them, and supplication, humble entreaty, and fear lest they become like them in many matters
in performing zakat, charities, maintaining kinship ties, and doing acts of goodness.”

key_terms.الزَّكَاةِ: the obligatory alms-tax given from wealth
key_terms.الْفُقَرَاءِ: the poor who are sustained through zakat
key_terms.الْمُوَاسَاةِ: mutual assistance and sharing with others

ai.seo_question: Why did Allah make zakat obligatory according to Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith explains that zakat was made obligatory to sustain the poor, protect the wealth of the rich, and cultivate gratitude, mercy, and patience. It also interprets the Qur'anic testing in wealth as giving zakat, presenting zakat as both a social duty and a moral lesson for the wealthy concerning the needs of this world and the Hereafter.
